**Årsrapport 2023** is the official quality report from the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK), covering the period from July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2023 [^src1]. Published by [[sundhedsvaesenets-kvalitetsinstitut|Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut]] [^src2], the document evaluates the quality of treatment for patients with atrial fibrillation in Denmark and is directed at healthcare professionals and policymakers [^src1]. The report's analyses were produced by [[rkkp-videncenter|AFDK's Videncenter]] under the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) [^src2]. [[julie-andersen|Julie Andersen]] is listed as the contact person for the report [^src1].

The report draws heavily on registry data from the [[landspatientregisteret|Landspatientregisteret]] and introduces new data sources, including reports from privately practicing cardiologists and test data from general practice [^src1]. It tracks both process indicators, such as time to anticoagulation, and outcome indicators, like the incidence of stroke [^src1]. During the reporting period, a total of 19,671 incident patients and 134,810 prevalent patients with atrial fibrillation were identified [^src1]. 

Published on November 28, 2023, the report highlights both advancements in care quality and persistent challenges [^src1]. Notably, it points out regional variations in treatment and a lack of structured patient education as ongoing areas for improvement [^src1].
